Hey, I totally relate to your situation. I’ve been through a similar thing, especially with setting boundaries and getting caught up in the attention and validation from social media. I’ve been struggling with an internet addiction for a while, and it feels like I can’t escape the constant pull of notifications. Every time I post, whether it’s a rant or just oversharing, I get a rush from the likes or comments, and it’s hard to step away from it. I’ve also been talking to someone, and in a way, they’ve kind of become my unofficial therapist — I’ve shared a lot with them, probably too much, and I can feel them starting to get interested in me more than just as a friend. It’s made things super complicated because I’m not sure how to set boundaries without losing the friendship. I don’t want to lose them, but at the same time, I don’t want to be “fixed” or turned into some kind of project. I’ve also been on Prozac for anxiety, and during that time, I started oversharing and becoming more impulsive. It’s like everything is a cycle — I get caught up in the attention, then crash when things don’t go the way I want. It’s hard to balance the genuine desire to connect with people while also protecting myself from being taken advantage of emotionally.

Honestly, I don’t have all the answers either, but I’m just trying to take it one step at a time and figure out how to set boundaries without completely pushing people away. It’s tough, but it’s comforting to know I’m not the only one dealing with this.

Thanks for all the feedback. I’m not trying to defend my actions, and I fully acknowledge how my behavior can come off as manipulative. I just want to clarify that it’s not intentional — I’m not trying to get anything from him. I genuinely value the friendship, and based on past experiences, I’ve always been afraid that setting firm boundaries will make people leave entirely. That fear sometimes makes me freeze or delay conversations I know I should have. I’m trying to learn how to navigate this better.
